note: sha256 is of the PRISTINE upstream bytes. vendored-diff.spec.ts reconstructs them from the vendored file by stripping the provenance header block through headerSentinel plus one blank line, then inverting intendedDivergence and then deltas - last applied, first inverted. A DELTA is a mechanical rewrite forced by vendoring: an import path that cannot resolve in the flat vendor layout. An INTENDED DIVERGENCE is a deliberate behaviour change HANGAR chose (D-02), and carries the reason, the plan that chose it and a date. Both lists are inverted before hashing, so upstream's sha256 still rules: a change that is in neither list still moves the hash and still names the file. The field is written out as an empty array where there is no divergence, so a reader can tell 'none' from 'a field nobody added'.

deltas.vendored: export type RGB = { r: number; g: number; b: number };

intendedDivergence.reason: The comment claimed a start of 255 makes the fade "always end dark". It does not, and the claim is what hid the defect: firmware freezes a cell at start - step*ticks, every step*ticks in this table is 248..254, so a start of 255 freezes 1..7 of 255 lit and nothing ever clears it. Corrected in the same plan that corrects the three codegen sites below, because a comment that contradicts the code it sits on is worse than no comment. NOTE FOR A RE-SYNCER, recorded here because it is the decision this row's arithmetic implies and does not make: the sibling touch kinds `bloom` and `disturb` carry a worse form of the same defect (residue up to 125, against comet's 1..7) and are DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE. Their repair needs a per-cell timeout derived from a per-cell start - a change to the emitted SHAPE, not to an emitted constant - and HANGAR's D-02 permission covers constants. Measured: no HANGAR preset selects either kind and touch.kind is not exposed as a knob, so neither is reachable from any catalog entry at any knob position. HANGAR's standing rule from plan 11-04 onward is that a HANGAR-owned preset must never select `bloom` or `disturb`.

case "comet": the emitted decay start. A decaying layer walks pha += fre on a uint8_t and freezes where the timeout catches it, so it lands on 0 only when the start equals step*ticks. 255 is odd and every emitted step is even for most rows, so 255 can never be reached: measured, every cell a finger crossed on AURORA, STARFIELD, RADAR and DIAL froze at phase 3 of 255 permanently - the bench report's "leaves a redish glow behind even when it disappeared". Emitting (256 - rate) * ticks lands the walk on exactly 0. Every value in DECAY_TABLE gives a three-digit start (248..254), so this is +0 characters at every reachable trailMs and no preset's declared cost moves. The `return paintCells` line is carried in this row because the glpfs line alone occurs twice in this file.

case "perFinger": the same emitted decay start as the comet row above, and the same arithmetic - measured, PINWHEEL froze one cell at phase 3 of 255 after a single slow tap. +0 characters. The preceding glc line is carried in this row because the glpfs line differs from the comet site only in indentation, and a row quoting it alone would match twice and correctly turn vendored-diff.spec.ts red.

The spring re-park comet inside sendsPaint's joystick path: when a sprung xy pad's contact ends, the home cell is repainted with the same decaying pair, so it carries the same permanent residue and takes the same fix. It is real codegen and not a cost estimate - src/vendor/botor/tests/pad.test.js pins the exact string it emits - so leaving it behind would have made a sprung joystick the one configuration whose parked dot still stuck. nearestDecay is called three times in one template rather than hoisted, because hoisting would move bytes this record would then have to justify for no behavioural gain. +0 characters.

intendedDivergence.upstream:
const ENDED = "e==3 or e>=5";
const LIVE = "e~=3 and e<5";
intendedDivergence.reason: Class B, the fast tap, at the one LIVE interpolation site. Firmware coalesces a sub-cycle press-and-lift into a single message with event code 9, and `e<5` is false for 9, so a tap ran no live path at all. Measured before the change, through the real Lua VM: PINWHEEL's perFinger layer record after a fast tap was pha 0 / fre 0 / timeout 0 where a slow press wrote 207 / 250 / 34 - the trail simply did not exist. +7 characters. This row first read "pinwheel has 596 free of 908 at its worst knob position": 596 is 908 minus the DEFAULTS cost (312), not a worst-position figure. Plan 11-04 measured the worst reachable knob position at 317, 591 free, and plan 11-06 then gave the card an xy stream, after which the 11-16 gate's reachability sweep reads worst 486, 422 free. Corrected by plan 11-16 on 2026-09-10. ENDED IS DELIBERATELY BYTE-UNCHANGED and the comment says why at length: all ten of its sites are release paths where code 9 genuinely IS an end, and the naive fix - making ENDED false for 9 - would leave a claimed finger slot, a dial baseline, a spring and a trackpad contact armed forever. LIVE is edited in place rather than shadowed by a second constant because it has exactly one interpolation site, so a new constant would have one user and leave a dead original beside it.

The simulator's mirror of _pad.ts's LIVE, moved in the same plan for the same reason: the preview and the device are two implementations of one behaviour, and fixing only the compiler would have left the preview showing nothing where the device now paints a trail. intendedDivergence.reason: The simulator's mirror of _pad.ts's phaseCond held arm, moved in the same plan. Without it the preview would show RADAR, JOYSTICK and FADERS ignoring a fast tap that the device now answers - the same fidelity loss D-02 forbids, arrived at from the other side. The press arm is left alone here exactly as it is left alone in the compiler, so the two files still say the same thing about the arm nobody can reach.

The expectation follows the codegen it pins. This line asserts the exact Lua the joystick spring re-park emits, and _pad.ts's spring row now emits a start of 252 rather than 255 at the default 420 ms trail. It is a vendored file under this manifest, so repairing its expectation is a divergence of its own rather than a free consequence, and it is recorded as one. No test is added or removed: this suite's count stays at 176.

The expectation follows the simulator it pins. The comet layer now starts at 252 rather than 255, so the frame after one tick reads 246 rather than 249. The comment moves with the numbers because it states the arithmetic in full and would otherwise contradict the assertion two lines below it. The tick ORDER this test exists to pin - the touch popped before the LED pass, so one increment has already been applied - is unchanged, and that is the whole point of the row: only the start moved.

THE VENDORED SUITE PINNED THE BUG. This line asserted that a comet cell freezes at phase 3 of 255 after its timeout expires - which is exactly the permanent residue the bench reported as AURORA's "redish glow" - and it asserted it as correct behaviour. With the start emitted as step*ticks the walk lands on 0 in exactly `ticks` steps, so the expectation becomes 0. Nothing about the freeze-on-expiry semantics changed; the cell still freezes, it now freezes dark.

The regular expression that reads AURORA's decay pair out of the compiled Lua carries the start as a literal, so it stops matching when the codegen emits 252. Deliberately still a literal rather than (\d+): this test's whole design is anti-drift - it takes the rate and ticks from the emitted Lua rather than from DECAY_TABLE so both sides cannot misread the table the same way - and widening the start to a capture group would remove the one number that pins the fix.
The same literal start, in the regular expression that reads the joystick spring re-park out of RADAR's compiled Lua. Kept a literal for the same anti-drift reason as the row above.

The spring re-park's phase after one tick, derived in the test from the start plus the rate read out of the compiled Lua. The start is the one term the test states itself, so it moves with the codegen. The `& 255` is the uint8_t wrap the simulator reproduces from grid_led.c and it is NOT touched here or anywhere else in this plan.
